summary: Resolved DG-7 with docs/decisions.md ADR-012 (Inbound Arr Webhook Boundary) and implemented the authenticated, bounded inbound Arr webhook boundary in src/ArrTags/Webhooks. ArrTagsWebhookController is an anonymous plugin ControllerBase discovered by Jellyfin's plugin controller registration and exposes POST /ArrTags/Webhook/Sonarr and POST /ArrTags/Webhook/Radarr. It authenticates the X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret header through the ADR-005 webhook lease (SecretReference.WebhookAuthentication, TryAcquire(reference, configurationVersion), SecretLease.Matches constant-time comparison); a missing configuration, missing candidate, oversized candidate, rotated generation, and mismatch all fail closed with the same bounded 401 and no secret/header/body leakage. WebhookBodyReader enforces OperationalLimits.WebhookMaxPayloadBytes (default 256 KiB, range 4 KiB-4 MiB) before buffering and returns 413. WebhookEventParser is tolerant of unknown fields and casing and bounded in JSON depth and episode count; it maps only the event kind, upgrade flag, and provider record/file hints, rejects empty/malformed/truncated/wrong-shaped payloads with 400, and acknowledges an unsupported event kind with 202 and no work. The bounded, coalescing WebhookIntake suppresses duplicate/out-of-order/replayed deliveries within a short window and drops overflow without blocking; the hosted WebhookIntakeService resolves accepted events off the request path. WebhookReconciliationResolver performs bounded provider-record-to-Jellyfin resolution: it returns only the Jellyfin items already associated with the advertised provider record in the persisted metadata-state mapping for the resolved connection, bounded by ReconciliationBatchSize, so a payload item id is never permission and no Arr write or direct publication occurs. Resolved items are enqueued through the existing IWorkHintSink as the same bounded LibraryWorkHint work as every other trigger, so the worker re-reads current Jellyfin and Arr state. MetadataStateStore gained a bounded Enumerate accessor used only by the resolution; DI registers the resolver, intake, and hosted service after the work worker. No queue, worker, publication, recovery, freshness, or regeneration mechanic changed.

known_limitations: Provider-record-to-Jellyfin resolution is a bounded best-effort lookup: it scans at most OperationalLimits.ReconciliationBatchSize persisted metadata-state records and returns at most that many distinct Jellyfin item ids. A webhook for a record ArrTags has not yet associated with a Jellyfin item produces no hint; library events and periodic reconciliation remain authoritative for new or missed items. This boundary is recorded in ADR-012.

Replay handling is idempotent coalescing (short bounded in-memory window plus the existing work-queue coalescing), not a persistent nonce/replay store; repeating a delivery after the window is admitted but cannot duplicate publication because the worker re-reads current state and publication is fingerprint-gated and single-flight. Recorded in ADR-012.

The hosted intake resolves one accepted event at a time; a burst beyond the bounded intake capacity (256) drops the excess rather than growing, and the dropped deliveries are repaired by the authoritative periodic reconciliation.

Jellyfin 12 plugin controller discovery is relied upon from the pinned research finding (docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 2.2). No live Jellyfin host or host assembly directory was available in this environment, so the route/controller contract is pinned structurally (exported public ControllerBase, [ApiController], [AllowAnonymous], fixed [Route]/[HttpPost] templates) rather than by a live HTTP round-trip.

The webhook route administration flow is documented in ADR-012 (fixed route plus the existing PluginConfiguration.WebhookSecret slot and the X-ArrTags-Webhook-Secret custom header). No configuration UI/page was added, and secret persistence/access remains governed by ADR-005; no change was made to the ADR-005 secret model.

The parser maps a relevant event that advertises no usable provider record identifier to 400 WrongShape. Providers that change their payload shape may therefore be rejected safely rather than guessed; a version-pinned payload fixture and contract test against a live provider remain release-time validation items.
